feature: Phase 2b watchlist expansion with trigger, investigation, merge, and orchestration
problem: Phase 2 investigates only 3 must-examine candidates. When results are weak (no suspects, low confidence, no evidence), the 4 watchlist candidates go uninvestigated, potentially missing the bug-introducing commit.
proposed_solution: Conditional Phase 2b: trigger check on Phase 2 output, fresh-context investigation of watchlist candidates via RevisedScopedInvestigator reuse (synthetic TriageResult, reduced budget), 5-step merge algorithm combining P2+P2b suspects, final InvestigationResult.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Phase2bResult dataclass has suspects (list[Suspect]), tool_calls (int), turns (int), trigger_reason (str)
AC2: should_trigger_phase2b() returns (True, reason) for any of: no suspects, max_confidence < 0.6, no evidence_quotes on top suspect
AC3: should_trigger_phase2b() returns (False, 'watchlist_skipped') when all conditions clear
AC4: merge_suspects() deduplicates by SHA, takes max confidence, unions evidence_quotes, keeps longer mechanism
AC5: merge_suspects() caps output at 5 suspects, sorts by (grounded_quote_count DESC, confidence DESC)
AC6: merge_suspects() promotes 2b-only suspects above P2 when confidence > top_p2 + 0.15
AC7: build_phase2b_system_prompt() includes all watchlist SHAs and excludes must-examine SHAs
AC8: build_phase2b_system_prompt() includes Phase 2 best suspect as reference when available
AC9: run_phase2b() skips investigation and returns watchlist_skipped when trigger is false
AC10: run_phase2b() reuses RevisedScopedInvestigator with budget=8 calls, 4 turns when triggered
edge_cases: EC1: Phase 2 produced suspects but all have confidence exactly 0.6 — should NOT trigger (boundary)
EC2: Phase 2 and 2b produce same SHA with different evidence — merge unions quotes without duplicates
EC3: Empty watchlist in TriageResult — Phase 2b returns watchlist_skipped immediately
EC4: Phase 2b produces no suspects — merge degenerates to Phase 2 only
verification_method: pytest tests/test_phase2b.py — all tests pass with zero regressions on full suite
